rulings.title: The priority order (§2)
rulings.ruling:
Ruled (manager, 2026-09-26, under the owner's delegation): the recommendation becomes the register's order. N1-N4 are never traded. Then R0 Evidence > R1 B-safety > R2 B-plasticity > R3 flexibility, self-regulation and emergence where they serve B > R4 A-openness > R5 current-run performance > R6 cost and elegance.
(i) R3 ranks above R4 and wins ties only: a flexible option wins only if it passes R1 and is actually exercised, not pinned at a cap (C25).
(ii) R1 is a budget (ε, O2), not a lexicographic rule. Inside it R2 is maximised (the ADR form), and it is never satisfied by freezing the live learner (N2). R1 acts as a lock only where its harm cannot be measured within ε: poisoning (O5) and irreversible closures. Closures leave the tie-break and go to the owner (R4; e.g. O17).
(iii) One order for decisions and tests (C41).
Two clauses from the owner's operating model are written into the order:
- R0: a bad reading ends an arm's candidacy at the configuration read, never the path, and the ruling's next arm runs.
- N3: an explicit owner ruling (D2, D8, D16, Q-RUN-8's 3000, WORLD kept for A, the CPU rule) stands until a GPU result contradicts it, and that result goes to the owner.
The conflicts draft (A-openness above flexibility) is kept on record as the alternative. Defaults: none (a rule, not a lever). No lever default moves, because §4-§6 were already written under this order.
rulings.basis:
The owner ranks it: "B is a bigger priority than A, since the belief is that with B, we can add A later" and "Flexibility is what I'm looking for to enhance continual learning" (05 lines 13-22; notes/AGENT_STATE.md:90-95). Flexibility is named as a means to B, so it sits directly under B's two halves. It wins only ties, because an untested means must not outrank the end it serves. A-openness sits above R5 because a later measurement cannot reopen a closed door (§2 'Why this order').

"Without risking too much" bounds risk rather than forbidding it, so R1 is a budget. A lexicographic R1 would minimise risk by not learning, which fails B (N2, C26).

The two orders differ only when R0-R2 tie and a flexible option competes with an A-openness option. Listing §6's 'Rule used' column (C01-C45) shows R3 against R4 in exactly one row, C41 (the test order). Every other row resolves on R0, R1, R2, N1-N4, or on R4 as an irreversible closure (C43). So adopting (i) moves no ruling in §4-§6. A-openness is kept by built-OFF arms (N1), so a flexibility win cannot delete an A path.

The 'bad result' clause is the owner's own: "Just because one result was bad does not mean the entire path is impractical or impossible" (notes/AGENT_STATE.md:115-116).

Rules used: N3 (the owner's own ranking) and R0. The owner delegated it on 2026-09-26 ("You can resolve most of the questions"). Nothing here closes a door or overturns a ruling, so it is not escalated.

rulings.title: ε (per-area worst-case regression per session) and the cumulative creep budget
rulings.ruling:
Ruled, as provisional manager values adopted now:
- ε = 0.05 bits/byte per area per session.
- Creep budget = 0.10 bits/byte per area (2ε), measured against the release anchor.
Both are absolute.

Form:
- Worst area, never the mean.
- The per-session reference is the parent anchor, read cooled (NEW-04).
- The cumulative reference is the release anchor: the chain's base checkpoint (the end-of-training parent the first session resumes from), recorded in the lineage (NEW-08).
- An area first admitted after the release anchor is referenced to the first gated checkpoint that read it.
- An area arriving in the session is read on its plasticity gain (NEW-11), not against ε.
- The release anchor is re-cut only on the owner's word, because a re-cut resets the cumulative budget.

Status:
- SOFT (reported) in training runs, and the non-inferiority margin of every B-endpoint comparison (E1's guard, 04-Q1 note 2; the S0b re-read; C04).
- HARD in the `continue` preset (unbuilt).

Creep joins NEW-04's rollback triggers. Appendix B stated it, but the combination rule left it out. A creep breach, read on the control half against the release anchor, rolls back the session that crossed it. The same retry ladder applies (`DATA_REPLAY_SHARE` 0.40, then the core LR halved), with the same 3-rejection count (C34).

The probe is sized to ε by §8 5.1, never ε to the probe. At 4 areas that needs a per-half SE ≤ ε/3.08 = 0.016 bits/byte (NEW-02 note). Pre-registered consequences:
- If §8 5.4 reads a family-wise false-rollback rate above 5%, or power below 80% at ε, the probe is enlarged or more nuisance runs are pooled, and the reading is repeated. ε does not move.
- If benign sessions breach ε, the next arms run in order: the retry ladder, §8 5.2's other LR arms, NEW-09's tiered uptake, NEW-06's reservoir, NEW-11's remedies, then 'regulated'. ε is never widened automatically.

The alternatives stay built, OFF. The gate's budget form is a lever built with NEW-04: default 'absolute' (ON); 'noise' (k × the probe's SE, NEW-02's draft) and 'relative' (a fraction of the area's own gain since arrival, the fraction pre-registered when the arm first runs) are arms. The minimum detectable regression and each area's regression as a fraction of its own gain are printed beside every verdict.
rulings.basis:
ε turns the owner's "without risking too much" into a number. The owner has delegated it, and it is reversible: SOFT in every training run, HARD only in an unbuilt preset, and a rejected session keeps its weights as a named checkpoint and its material in the inbox (NEW-04 note).

Why 0.05:
(1) It is the toy's minimum detectable effect for the six-area mean at 5 paired seeds: (2.132 + 0.941) × 0.0385 / √5 = 0.053 (`rule_self_regulation/paired.py`, re-run here). The per-area toy MDEs are larger: 0.072 easy, 0.086 cred, 0.176 hard (same formula on the per-area SDs 0.0527, 0.0624 and 0.1279 from the same script's rows). So the per-area probe must be larger than the toy's, and §8 5.1 sizes it.
(2) It separates the regimes the tree has seen. Inside it: rehearsed retention +0.046 (D2, `.rework/DECISIONS.md:101-102`) and 25% replay at 1.936 → 1.931 (03 §9, CONTRACT-Q-DATA-7). Far outside it: pure-add +0.444 (8.9 × ε), tagged faded-area forgetting +0.28 to +0.31 (5.6-6.2 × ε) and never-tagged forgetting +1.23 to +1.87 (25-37 × ε) (C18). These are toy readings: a hypothesis about scale, not efficacy evidence.
(3) It is about 1.9% of a text model's bits/byte: 0.05 / 2.6892 = 0.0186, using the CPU S0b k0 seed-0 prequential reading for scale only (arithmetic).

The rehearsed toy's +0.046 uses 92% of ε (0.046 / 0.05). That is a signal that ε may bind on benign sessions. C26's plasticity-gain floor and escalate_if cover it.

Why absolute: a k × SE budget widens silently when probes are halved or areas are added (C04, critic blocking 1).

Why creep = 2ε: without a cumulative bound, per-session passes compound (N sessions allow N × ε). A release-anchor reading is one paired comparison on the fixed probe, so its noise does not compound; only one-directional drift accumulates, and 2ε admits at most two worst-case sessions of it. A best-ever reference is excluded because it ratchets toward a freeze (NEW-02 note).

Rules used: R1 (the budget), R0 (a GPU reading sizes the probe), N2.
rulings.deciding_test: §8 5.1 [GPU] sizes the probe to ε (per-window variance → windows per area per half at ≥ 80% power, ≤ 5% family-wise). §8 5.4 [GPU] validates both error rates at ε on benign and harmful sessions. Neither moves ε. The benign-session readings of §8 5.2, 5.4 and 5.6 [GPU] can bring it back (escalate_if). §8 4.1 [CPU: operation only] checks the harness.

rulings.title: The scope of the unreliability belief
rulings.ruling:
Ruled: the recommendation. The belief is tested on inputs, targets, sources and the system's own components. That means U-series families:
- (a) segmentation
- (b) `LM_DROPOUT`
- (c) tag drop
- (d) codec drift
- (e) dynamic mapping
- (f) liar and noise share
- (g) corrupted targets
- (h) structural unreliability: expert and route dropout, MEM retrieval dropout, `FAB_MUT` and `FAB_BIRTH_JITTER` levels, stamps and Levels OFF.

No default leans on the belief until R3 (held-out under a family left out of training) reads on GPU. Then the test sets the default (R0).

Defaults unchanged: `TOK_DROPOUT` 0 (OFF), `LM_DROPOUT` 0 (OFF), `FAB_MUT` 0.25 (ON), `FAB_BIRTH_JITTER` 0.15 (ON), stamps ON, Levels ON (DOM half built first; TREE-S0b-LEVELS), `DATA_TAG_DROP` per 04-Q13 (O7). Family (h)'s new perturbations (expert, route and MEM retrieval dropout) are built OFF (0) as phase-scheduled levers, each with a training-run value and a preset value.

Order inside §8 5.9: family (h)'s arms over the shipped-ON defaults (Levels, stamps, `FAB_MUT`, jitter) read first, then the rest in §2's order.

The pre-registered verdict is NEW-12's:
- Falsified (strong form) if R2 improves but no family at any level improves R1 or R3 beyond the paired-seed spread.
- Supported if a mixed-family arm improves R3 and R4 at equal compute.

A falsified first reading does not close the belief. The next tests, in order:
1. The replay regime wherever single-pass read (forms 1-2 depend on the regime, C21).
2. The self-regulated ADR variant, raising a family's level while ε holds.
3. Mixed-family arms.
4. Form 3 through the diversity pilot (§8 5.11) and family (e).
5. The owner-scale re-read (§8 6.7), since small-scale verdicts can invert with scale.

If the strong form is falsified, the belief is kept where it is supported: same-family invariance (§7.3).
rulings.basis:
The belief is the owner's (05 lines 21-22), and "unreliable system" reads most literally as the system's own components (critic major 6, Appendix A row 6). Testing inputs only (C24's draft) would leave that reading untested and narrow the owner's words.

A broader scope removes nothing and moves no default, so R0-R2 are untouched. Its cost is GPU runs: C41 counts 8 families × 4 levels × 5 seeds × 2 regimes = 320 runs with (h), against 7 × 4 × 5 × 2 = 280 without it. So (h) adds 40 runs, 12.5% (arithmetic).

The shipped-ON components in (h) have no efficacy evidence. `FAB_MUT` and jitter are ON for mechanical reasons (§7.1 form 5; `src/fabric/levers.py:686-713`); Levels are ON on known answers and arithmetic (TREE-S0b-LEVELS). So 5.9 is their only R0 reading, and an adverse reading returns them to OFF (TREE-S0b-LEVELS, C21). That is why they read first.

Stamps and Levels stay ON on R1 evidence (the CAP runaway, 2048 → 8192 in 19 lifts; spurious DOM spawns; C24), not on a scope argument.

CPU runs only check that the generators and harness operate (§8 4.9).

Rules used: R3 (the belief orders which arms are built and tested first), R0 (the test, not the belief, sets defaults), N1.

rulings.title: Which copy serves after training
rulings.ruling:
Ruled: the recommendation. After training, users are served by the last promoted, cooled checkpoint: the cooled branch that the session-end gate read and passed (NEW-04). FRAME (1) already runs cooldowns only on branch children used for evaluation, gating and serving.

How it works:
- The learner trains as a shadow.
- A session that passes the gate is promoted, and its cooled branch becomes the served copy.
- A rejected session changes nothing served: rollback restores the learner, and the served copy was never replaced.
- Serving reads admitted MEM entries only (C07). The memory-on served path stays OFF until measured (NEW-03), and T0 stays OFF (NEW-15).

Serving from the learner is kept, not removed. A serving lever is built with the serving path: 'promoted' (default, ON) and 'learner' (an OFF arm). What the 'learner' arm would expose is reported: the mid-session worst-area regression against ε, and the stability-gap depth, at each probe reading (already read in §8 5.2 and 5.4).

If one card cannot hold both copies, the first fallback is time-sharing (the promoted copy serves between sessions), not serving from the learner.

Nothing is built now: the tree has no inference path (§1). The lever lands with the serving path, after NEW-03's `EVAL.generate`. Appendix B gains a row.
rulings.basis:
R1 decides this without an efficacy test.

Mid-session, the learner has passed no gate. Only NonFinite or the blow-up Reading can stop a session before its end, and the verdict comes only at session end, after a settle window, on a cooled branch (NEW-04 note). Serving from the learner would expose users to uncooled states and to the stability-gap dip that every common method shows at a shift (TREE-OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM). Served outputs cannot be recalled, so that exposure is irreversible, and R1 requires a snapshot anchor before any irreversible change.

R2 is unaffected: the learner learns the same under either choice. Only the latency before learning reaches users changes, by one session.

NEW-01 already rejects learning in place in the serving copy as a default (irreversible between checkpoints).

Cost at today's shape: 04 §7's packing figure is 12 runs per 140 GiB card (`docs/proposals/04_SELF_REGULATION.md:1455`), about 11.7 GiB per training run (140 / 12, arithmetic). A served copy carries no optimizer state, so it fits beside the learner on the owner's card.

Rules used: R1 over R2's latency cost; N1 (the learner arm stays built).
rulings.deciding_test: none for the default (R1, a design ruling). §8 5.2 and 5.4 [GPU] report the mid-session worst-area regression and stability-gap depth that the 'learner' arm would expose. When the serving path is built, a CPU operation check: the served copy is bit-identical to the gate-read cooled branch, and a rollback leaves it untouched.
rulings.owner_ruling_touched: None explicit. It applies the fundamentals' "without risking too much" (05 line 15). The operating model (notes/AGENT_STATE.md:112-125) moves the [OWNER] tag to the manager. It depends on O10 (whether a gate may act on one session's reading), which it does not rule.
rulings.escalate_if:
(1) A proposal to make 'learner' the default serving copy, for example if §8 5.2/5.4 show every mid-session reading within ε and promotion latency becomes the binding cost. That changes users' exposure, which is a product choice.
(2) At a later scale one card cannot hold both copies, and time-sharing leaves too little time for sessions, so serving and learning compete for the card.
(3) The served copy cannot advance, because the gate may not act (O10) or rejects repeatedly (C34's 3 rejections). B then never reaches users.

rulings.title: The root of trust
rulings.ruling:
Decided by test; the lock holds meanwhile.

Interim (ON in the `continue` preset, which is unbuilt; training runs are unchanged):
- Untrusted input enters memory-first quarantine (NEW-07): a read-only side path; readable by evaluation and gates, not by served retrieval; tagged with origin and session.
- Only owner-trusted origins promote from quarantine to weights. They do so in a consolidation session, with the delay, a clean canary and the per-origin cap (NEW-18; the cap's value is O18).
- Owner-trusted origins are an explicit list in the preset (N4), never inferred from content. Default: the origins of the parent's training manifest and the four `data/continual/` corpora (01_rust, 02_sawyer, 03_dracula, 04_num2). The owner adds an origin by naming it.
- Owner-trusted material declared as a session's new material trains in that session (NEW-01). Quarantine is for everything else.
- Unpromoted material is never deleted.
- The unlocked alternative (any origin promotes after the delay, bounded by caps and canaries) is built and run as §8 5.7's OFF arm. It never becomes the default before the rule below passes.

Pre-registered rule: the lock opens for corroboration by ≥ 2 SR6-certified independent origins (NEW-18) when all three read:
(1) SR6 copy detection returns the known answers on E5's majority-false and 50%-impersonation worlds, model-free (§8 0.6 [CPU]; operation, a precondition only).
(2) E5 on 'focusbed' with SR6 on meets 04's pre-registered eligibility in those worlds: `format_split_floored` 0 in every world, and the majority-false world loses at most 0.1 Qc accuracy (`docs/proposals/04_SELF_REGULATION.md:1510`) [GPU, §8 6.2].
(3) §8 5.7 [GPU], with SR6-certified corroboration as the promotion rule, 5 seeds, k ∈ {5, 25, 100} poisoned documents from one origin, split across 2-5 colluders, and from an impersonator. It passes if no canary trips beyond its nuisance-calibrated threshold (NEW-04's canary trigger, calibrated in §8 5.1) at any k, split or seed, and if benign material from a genuine new origin is promoted within one session of its delay.

If (2) or (3) fails, the lock holds and the next arm runs, each re-read on 5.7:
(i) Promotion delay of 2, then 4 sessions (C35's discovery ladder 1/2/4), with the canary re-read before promotion.
(ii) A smaller per-origin cap, stepped by E5's fixed-count-poison world (04-Q12).
(iii) The trust-weighted loss arm.
(iv) The filtering-only arm (NEW-07).
Anchor retention stays ON throughout (C35, 8 sessions).
rulings.basis:
Here R1 acts as a lock, not a budget, and the lock is the safer interim for three reasons.
(a) Poisoning is not measurable within ε. A backdoor stays invisible to the per-area probe until its trigger appears, so the gate cannot bound it; canaries and the SR6 lock are R1's instrument there (C05).
(b) It is irreversible past the anchors. Removing poison from weights afterwards is unreliable (04-Q12), and the ring holds 1-2 generations (C35). The literature's fixed count, about 250 documents at 600M-13B, does not shrink with clean volume (§7.1 form 4).
(c) Collusion defeats agreement. Majority-false inverted trust at 3 of 3 seeds, and 50% impersonation flipped it (04-Q12, C05). These are toy readings, which order the GPU tests and prove nothing.

The lock costs B nothing in the near term:
- Every B test in §8 Stages 5-6 trains on owner-trusted corpora (the session chain's `data/continual/`).
- An open-ended inbox first needs the look-ahead draw and record compaction (C36).

It defers untrusted learning and never deletes it (N1). Quarantined material stays readable by evaluation and gates, and the observe-mode trust book reads it (04-6.3), so source credibility stays observable. The emergent, ungated path is kept as the logged OFF arm (C29).

Why a test decides the opening: whether copy detection makes corroboration safe is an efficacy question, so under the CPU rule it reads on GPU (5.7, 6.2). The register's earlier wording (SR6 passing E5's worlds) is kept as the CPU precondition.

Rules used: R1 over R2 and R3 (C05); R0 for the opening; N1.
rulings.deciding_test: §8 5.7 [GPU]: canaries from one origin, 2-5 colluders and an impersonator; SR6-certified corroboration against the unlocked arm. With §8 6.2 [GPU]: E5's majority-false and 50%-impersonation worlds with SR6 on. §8 0.6 and 4.7 [CPU: operation only] are preconditions.

No explicit ruling. The owner's standing preferences (notes/AGENT_STATE.md:48-50):
- Context awareness, including the credibility of sources, is what the lock actuates on. Provenance (NEW-08) and the observe-mode trust book (04-6.3) stay ON.
- Emergence preferred: the ungated path is kept as an arm and read (C29).
It depends on O18 (the cap's value) and O10 (the consolidation gate acting), neither ruled here.
rulings.escalate_if:
(1) Every arm of the ladder fails §8 5.7 on GPU, so the lock cannot open. B's learning from the open world then stays limited to owner-trusted origins, a limit on "continually learn" that the owner should weigh: widen the trusted list, or accept a residual risk.
(2) Any GPU run shows a promoted canary that rollback cannot remove within the anchor-retention horizon (C35, 8 sessions). That is a B-safety failure of the lock itself.

rulings.title: The continue preset's continuation learning rate (`OPT_LR_CONTINUE`)
rulings.ruling: Decided on GPU by §8 5.2 under the rule below. No human reading is needed. Interim, while the shipped behaviour holds: the lever `OPT_LR_CONTINUE` defaults to 'as_logged', ON everywhere. That is today's pricing, and the regime is printed as `opt.continue.regime`. 'floor', 'plateau' (`OPT_LR_PLATEAU` 0.1 / 0.25), 'rewarm' (`OPT_LR_REWARM` 0.5 / 1.0) and 'regulated' are built OFF as arms, with `OPT_LR_CONT_WARM` 1000. The continue preset carries no `OPT_LR_CONTINUE` value and does not ship until 5.2 reads. Stage 5 rows that run after 5.2 inherit its winner. Any continuation run before then (harnesses, measurement-protocol resumes) runs 'as_logged' and states its regime in its label: the floor for a revision-log parent, the re-priced rate for a k0 parent. Pre-registered rule: 5 paired seeds on the NEW-01 session chain (base, then four sessions), read on cooled branches from the report halves. (1) An arm is admissible when ACC is within ε, read as NEW-02 reads it (worst area, never the mean). At every session end, every area's regression against the parent anchor must have its one-sided 95% upper bound below ε, and the cumulative regression against the release anchor must stay within the creep budget. ε and creep are as set under O2; the recommended values are 0.05 and 0.10 bits/byte. (2) Among the admissible fixed arms (floor, plateau 0.1, plateau 0.25, rewarm 0.5, rewarm 1.0), the preset takes the arm with the largest new-area gain: the new area's bits/byte drop over its session, averaged over the four sessions. A difference counts only if it is significant (one-sided paired t, α 0.05). A tie goes to the arm with the smaller worst-area regression and is reported with its 90% interval (C25). The LR arms run at the preset's interim values of the other levers (`OPT_BORN_CLOCK` ON, the clip at the parent's p99, tiered uptake, `DATA_DRAW` 'replay' 0.27, `DATA_REHEARSE_PARENT` True; Appendix B). 5.2's secondary pairs (born clocks, clip, uptake, `OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM`) then run on the winner. (3) Once the gate is built (§8 5.4), 'regulated' runs against the fixed winner. It takes the preset if it is admissible, is not significantly worse on new-area gain, and actually regulates: its session plateau sits at a bound of its range in fewer than 16 of 20 session-readings (0.8 × 4 sessions × 5 seeds, arithmetic; the form of 04-Q2 (c)). (4) If no arm is admissible, the preset stays unshipped at 'as_logged' and the next arms run in order, each under the same rule: 5.2's secondary levers on the lowest-regression arm; `DATA_REPLAY_SHARE` 0.40 (the NEW-04 retry value, E1's arm); NEW-11's remedies in order (L2 toward the anchor first, §8 5.6); 'regulated' after 5.4. If 'floor' wins it is adopted. Every arm stays built and 'as_logged' stays the lever default (N1).
rulings.basis: R0 and the owner's CPU rule. Which rate lets the model learn after training within ε is an efficacy question, so only a GPU reading sets the preset value. R1 as a budget, with R2 maximised inside it, gives the rule's form: admissible within ε, then the largest new-area gain. That form is O6's recommendation and C01's ruling (§3.3 l.320; C01 l.978; NEW-05 l.847). The alternative, fixing 'plateau' 0.25 now, sets a default with no GPU reading. The constant 2e-3 pilots all turned upward after about 6000 steps (Q-OPT-3, INV-28, confounded; note FRAME-POST-TRAINING l.667-675), so no rate is presumed safe. The register's owner-reason was that only the owner can accept 'floor' lowering a k0 parent's rate. That is answered without the owner. First, a preset value chosen on B's endpoints removes no functionality: all five arms and 'as_logged' stay reachable (N1). Second, on the shipped-default parent 'floor' changes nothing: every k3000 parent past window 3000 carries a revision log and already resumes at the floor, 0.05 of peak (§3.1 item 5, l.224-239). 'floor' lowers only a k0 parent's rate, from 0.2173 of peak at 3.78 MB and 0.4759 at 756 KB to 0.05 (`results/decisions_2026-09-26/verify/emp3/k0child_378MB_s0.out`, `k0child_756KB_s0.out`, checked). The tie-break to the smaller worst-area regression follows C25 (B's endpoints decide) and 04-Q2 (a tie in the mean with worse tails is not neutral for B). The next-arm ladder applies the owner's 'one bad result does not end the path', and every rung already exists in the register (NEW-09, C02, C42, NEW-04's retry ladder, NEW-11). §8 4.2 on CPU checks only that each arm starts at its intended rate (operation). C39 sequences these arms before E2 and E1, and E1 shape (e) inherits the winner (note 04-Q1 item 4, l.542-546).

rulings.title: Source tags: tagged retention against untagged served use, and the drop value
rulings.ruling: Decided on GPU by E4 (§8 6.6) under the rule below. No human reading is needed. Interim, while the shipped default holds: `DATA_TAG` 'off' (OFF); `DATA_TAG_DROP` 0.25 (built, inert while OFF); `LM_SRC_AT` 'input'. 'area', 'domain' and 'head' stay built arms (04-Q13). The tag comes from provenance, never from content, and document ids stay in the provenance books (`Stream.sources`). The trade is settled by R1 used as a budget. The untagged regression on served prompts of unknown origin is the budget, bounded by ε: by the owner's own O2 definition, a regression within ε is not 'too much'. Tagged worst-area retention is maximised inside that budget. Pre-registered rule, over every configuration E4 runs (id 'area' / 'domain'; drop 0 / 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5; entry 'input' / 'head'): 5 paired seeds, whole-epoch sizing (§8 0.4), each area's forgetting from the end of its last live phase to run end, report halves, against the never-tagged model. (1) A configuration is admissible when both hold. (a) Untagged cost: the worst-area untagged bits/byte difference has its one-sided 95% upper bound below ε. (b) Tagged gain: never-tagged minus tagged-read worst-area forgetting has a paired mean above ε, and the improvement is significant (one-sided paired t against 0, α 0.05). (2) If any configuration is admissible, `DATA_TAG` goes ON at the admissible configuration with the smallest tagged worst-area forgetting. A tie (not significant at α 0.05; reported with its 90% interval) goes to the higher drop, for invariance to a missing tag (C19). A remaining tie goes to 'head' if `fab.expert_area_purity` or `mem.hit_area_purity` rises significantly with the tag on at 'input' (label-driven structure; 04 §8 Q13, C33), and otherwise to 'input'. (3) If no configuration is admissible, `DATA_TAG` stays 'off' (still built), both sides' numbers are recorded in the register, and the next arms run under the same rule. (i) If (b) passes, (a) fails, and the untagged cost falls with drop across the ladder, the ladder is extended above 0.5, with its rung pre-registered before the run. (ii) Tags run on the session chain in the continue preset, where session material carries provenance and the gate reads the untagged served path. (iii) U-series family (c) reads the drop ladder with R3 (§8 5.9).
rulings.basis: Both sides are R1 (§3.3 O7, l.321; C18, l.995), so the order alone cannot rank them. The owner's ε (O2) can, because it is the owner's definition of 'too much'. An untagged cost within ε is therefore acceptable by definition. A cost beyond ε on the served path is too much whatever the tagged gain, because prompts of unknown origin carry no tag. That is R1 as a budget (§2), the form O1 recommends. It replaces E4's untagged-only rule (`docs/proposals/04_SELF_REGULATION.md:1509`), which ignored retention. The toy shows why both sides are read. A tag at read cut the faded easy area's forgetting to +0.28 to +0.31 bits/byte, against +1.23 to +1.87 never-tagged (C18, `d2/forget_tag.py`): a paired gain of 0.95-1.56 bits/byte at 3 of 3 seeds (arithmetic from C18's per-seed values). The untagged cost was +0.051 (t 2.56), and drop 0 kept tagged retention best (+0.15 to +0.25). These are toy readings and so hypotheses only: the gain sits far beyond ε while the cost sits at the recommended ε, which is why the drop ladder and the entry point are where E4 turns. The tie-break to the higher drop follows C19 and §7.2 (tag dropout is justified by invariance to a missing tag, l.1055). 'head' on label-driven structure follows 04's own rule and C33 (B over A, then label-free routing). Context awareness is not lost while tags are OFF: provenance books, observe-mode trust, per-origin caps and quarantine carry source credibility without the model's input tag (NEW-07, 04-6.3). The status quo OFF holds until the GPU reading (R0, NEW-19).

rulings.title: 04-Q2: does a statistical tie go to the self-regulated draw?
rulings.ruling: Conditional yes, fixed before E1 runs; 04-Q2's (a)-(d) are unchanged in substance. A tie goes to 'retention' only if all four hold. (a) It passes 04-Q1's per-area guard at ε. (b) It is a tie on E1's primary endpoint: within ε on the time-integrated gap and not significantly different (one-sided paired t, α 0.05, 5 paired seeds). Significantly better wins outright and significantly worse loses (C25). (c) It actually regulates: last-phase `data.focus.rho_at_cap_frac` is below 0.8, or `data.focus.alloc_freedom` is at least 0.2 after normalising by its maximum under the floors in force (C17), with the raw value reported beside it. (d) Its compute is charged through `replay_cm`. If (c) fails, the tie goes to the hand-set arm it tied with; 04-Q2 names 'replay', the arm expected there. Every tie is reported with its 90% interval and never read as equivalence: at 5 seeds a tie is a difference below the minimum detectable effect, about 0.042 bits/byte on the time-integrated gap (`paired.py`, note l.582-586). Defaults are unchanged: `DATA_DRAW` 'planned' (D8), with 'replay' (SR0) and 'retention' (SR2) built OFF. The same form governs every tie the register breaks toward the flexible or self-regulated option (C25: E1, E2, the retok fleet).

The alternative, 'a tie keeps the simpler hand-set arm', is an R6 argument (cost and elegance). R3 ranks above R6 under both O1 alternatives: the conflicts draft put flexibility at its R4, still above current-run performance and cost. So O8 does not wait on O1. The owner states the preference directly: 'a part of my beliefs are for the system's self regulation for a large part of it' (`docs/proposals/04_SELF_REGULATION.md:16-18`), and 'Flexibility is what I'm looking for to enhance continual learning' (§1, l.107). The conditions keep the preference honest. (a) is R1. (c) refuses to credit a controller pinned at its cap: on the toy, ρ sat at its cap in 26-47 of 48-49 last-phase re-plans in the retention arms (`verify/emp3/toy_stats.out`, §3.2 l.285). (d) charges its 4.3%+ wall (04-Q2 l.515). The residual risk (C25) is that low-powered ties mostly go to the flexible option; the 90% interval and guard (a) bound it.

rulings.title: PLAN 3.8 and the instrument line: may a control act on one run's reading?
rulings.ruling: PLAN 3.8 governs verdicts, not control actions. Its text is 'No comparison may be reported from fewer than two seeds; every Reading carries its seed count; the renderer refuses to print a verdict on n=1' (`.rework/PLAN.md:140-143`). It is a rule about reported comparisons, and it stands for them unchanged: default changes, reported conclusions and findings keep ≥ 2 seeds, with the seed count printed. A control action that consumes a held-out Reading may act on one run (n = 1) when all three conditions hold. (i) Logged: the Reading with its `seed_count`, the threshold, the action and its outcome are counted and printed. (ii) Reversible: it defers or diverts learning and deletes nothing (N1). A rollback restores a whole generation from a kept anchor (C09); rejected material stays in the inbox tagged 'rejected'; the rejected weights stay as a named checkpoint (NEW-04). (iii) Bounded by a budget calibrated on multi-seed nuisance runs: every threshold that fires it is set from the null distribution of the maximum over areas (§8 5.1), for ≤ 5% family-wise false actions and ≥ 80% power at ε (NEW-02). Held-out readings cross the instrument line backwards only as declared wires carrying a Reading with its seed count, as `d_best_bpb` already does (`src/eval/levers.py:146-149`). Controls read only the control half of each held-out block and verdicts only the report half (C11), so no action grades itself. Defaults: the session gate is SOFT (report only) in training runs. In the continue preset it is HARD once §8 5.1's calibration exists, and report-only before that (thresholds provisional, Appendix B). Mid-session, only NonFinite or the blow-up Reading stops a session (NEW-04). `CKPT.Retention.consider`, an additive save (`CKPT_BEST_KEEP_TOL` 0.02), acts at n = 1 once fed (04-Q10). OPT's restart damping stays refused at `seed_count` 1, as built: `src/opt/api.py:539-561`, counted by `opt.restart.damp_refused_n1`, with `OPT_DAMP_SOURCE` 'off' and 'probe' an arm. No calibrated budget bounds damping yet, so the tree's reading that a damped restart is a verdict stands. A damping arm that meets (i)-(iii) is built behind its own lever, OFF, after §8 5.1. 'regulated' `OPT_LR_CONTINUE` (after 5.4) and the 'retention' draw are control actions under the same conditions, and they act only in their arms until a GPU reading makes them defaults. If §8 5.4 reads above 5% family-wise false rollbacks, or below 80% power at ε, the preset's gate stays HARD, because a false rollback defers learning and deletes nothing. Meanwhile the next arms run in order: a larger probe (priced under R1, O11), W 2×, then graded rollback in place of hard (NEW-04).
rulings.basis: C30 (l.1007) states the collision. OPT already refuses to damp at seed_count 1, so if PLAN 3.8 covers gates, a session gate can never act: every session is one run of one learner, and its reading has seed_count 1. That reading would leave B with no acting safety mechanism after training. R1's budget ε could then be reported but never enforced, and 'without risking too much' would rest on nothing. rulings.title: Monitoring floors against wall-time caps
rulings.ruling:
The principle is ruled now; the numbers are ruled by the GPU. Monitoring is priced under R1 (C31). Every monitor has a floor, and a wall-time cap applies only above that floor. No cap may thin a monitor below its floor, or shrink a probe below its ε-sized n. The floors are: the retention probe takes at least 5 readings per phase, counting the phase-start reading (04-6.2); in gated sessions the probe cadence is at most a third of the shortest stamp interval (C03); a codec probe reads at every refresh, with paired SE at most `AUD_RATE_TOL` / 2 (03b-16.30); at least 1 trust pass per session and per N bytes of a new origin (C31, O18); and at least 1 plasticity-gain reading per session (NEW-11).

INTERIM VALUES (unchanged; they already follow the principle):
- Training runs: `EVAL_RETENTION_EVERY` 1000 plus a phase-start reading. It is ON after SR0's bit-identity test and 0 until then, because the probe is unbuilt. Each pre-registration writes its own cap as a number: the shortest phase's windows / 5, about 700 at k3000 on the 3.78 MB shape (N4).
- `continue` preset (unbuilt): 1000 in text sessions at k3000; 333 at k1000 and in media sessions at k3000; 667 for media at k0.
- Probe size: 6 windows per area until §8 5.1 reads.
- Plasticity gain probe: OFF until §8 5.6.
- E6's 2% cap and E3's 2% cap bind only above the floor.

PRE-REGISTERED RULE. Inputs: §8 5.1 gives n_ε, the windows per area per half needed for at least 80% power at ε with at most 5% family-wise false rollbacks (NEW-02). E6 (§8 6.2) then measures on GPU the wall share w_F of the floor cadence F at n_ε. F is the sparsest cadence that meets every floor above. It is measured at the whole-epoch shape and at the session shape.
(1) If w_F ≤ 2%: E6 picks the densest cadence at or above F that costs at most 2% (04-6.2 unchanged).
(2) If w_F > 2%: the cadence is F. The cap does not bind (R1 over R6), and w_F is printed beside every verdict. The cost arms below are then read in order. An arm is adopted only if §8 5.4's injected-harm sessions show the same miss rate at ε and at most 5% family-wise false rollbacks:
  (a) the probe forward runs batched and gradient-free on the read-only side path (C06);
  (b) stamp-aligned readings replace C03's third-of-interval cadence at scheduled stamps (TOK acts and AUD refreshes): one reading just after each stamp and one just before the next. In a media session at k3000 the 2000∪3000 union stamps at 2000, 3000, 4000 and 6000 in each 6000 windows, so this takes 2 × 4 = 8 readings against 6000 / 333 ≈ 18 (arithmetic). At k1000 it takes 2 per interval against 3;
  (c) the probe is split across consecutive readings, and the gate pools the settle segment's readings at session end (NEW-04).
  The cheapest arm that passes sets the preset value. An arm that fails stays built, OFF.
(3) The same rule prices the plasticity probe (§8 5.6), trust passes (E3) and codec probes (§8 7.1). `CKPT_EVERY` in the preset keeps matching the chosen cadence.

Never allowed: thinning below a floor, or dropping n below n_ε, to meet a cap (N1).
rulings.basis:
- C31 already resolves the principle: monitoring is priced under R1, floors hold, and caps apply above them. R1 outranks R6 and R5.
- N1: a monitor is deferred or made cheaper, never dropped.
- What is unknown is the size of the collision. The §3.3 arithmetic is 4 areas × 6 windows / 333 = 7.2% extra forward windows, which is 2.1-2.4% of wall (7.2/3 = 2.4 at forward ≈ 1/3 step; 7.2 × 4.3/15 = 2.1 on the toy's wall basis). That is only a lower bound, because it scales linearly with the ε-sized probe, and that probe exists only after §8 5.1's per-window variance reads on GPU (note NEW-02: 'no such reading exists yet').
- Under R0 and the CPU rule, only E6's GPU wall measurement can set the cadence.
- The cost arms are ordered so that power at ε (NEW-02, C04) is never traded for throughput. Each arm is accepted on the gate's own error rates (§8 5.4), not on a judgement call.
- The preset values stay numbers written by the builder (N4).
rulings.deciding_test: §8 5.1 [GPU] (n_ε) then §8 6.2 [GPU] (E6 measures w_F at the floor); §8 5.4 [GPU] accepts or rejects each cost arm; §8 5.6 [GPU] and §8 7.1 [GPU] price the plasticity and codec probes under the same rule

rulings.escalate_if:
- After cost arms (a)-(c), the floors at n_ε still cost more wall than the training they monitor: w_F > 50% of wall (arithmetic: monitoring m exceeds training t exactly when m / (m + t) > 0.5). That would halve the throughput of every B fleet and session.
- Or the only remaining way to meet a cost would loosen ε or a floor. That trades B-safety for throughput on the owner's own definition of 'too much' (O2).

THE CONTRACT'S OPEN LIST, RULED:
(i) The forecast magnitude bound is built as a lever before §8 6.5. It is inert and bit-identical while feedback is OFF. In every feedback-on arm it is ON at 10 × ‖h‖ per position (provisional: the instability signature).
(ii) WORLD's own objectives stay. `pop(z).detach()` into `world_proj` is not built while feedback is OFF; it is built OFF, as an arm, beside any feedback flip.
(iii) Aligning MEM's keys with h + forecast is an arm only once feedback is ON and `MEM.blend` lands. With feedback OFF, FAB, the readout and MEM all see h alone, so nothing is misaligned.

NEW LEVER, built before §8 6.5 (N1, N4): WORLD's input gradient.
- Default 'attached', which is today's behaviour: WORLD's losses reach LM.embed through the undetached obs_emb.
- Arm 'detached': WORLD reads LM.embed's output through a stop-gradient. It keeps its objectives and keeps learning, but no longer shapes the LM.
- CPU known answers: at 'attached' bit-identical to today; at 'detached' WORLD's gradient on `emb.weight` reads exactly 0 while WORLD's own tensors still move.

§8 6.5 runs 5 arms (fb_off, fb_on, skip, world_off, detached) × 5 paired seeds = 25 runs, against 20 before (+25%, arithmetic). All arms are in one post-SR0 commit as note WORLD pre-registers, with `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` pinned (O14). Endpoints: the worst-area time-integrated held-out gap on SR0's probe (report half). The end-state per area and both prequential endpoints (last half, full run) are reported beside it.

(A) `WORLD_ENABLED`. Let C = fb_off − world_off on the worst area, as the paired mean over 5 seeds, at margin ε (O2).
  - If C ≤ ε: no change.
  - If C > ε: read C' = detached − world_off the same way. If C' ≤ ε, 'detached' becomes WORLD's default input gradient; WORLD stays ON for A, and 'attached' stays built as the arm.
  - If C' > ε too: WORLD stays ON (N3) and the readings go to the owner.
(B) `WORLD_FEEDBACK` flips ON only under note WORLD (4):
  (a) fb_on beats fb_off on the time-integrated all-area gap (one-sided paired t, α 0.05, 5 seeds);
  (b) fb_on is not worse than ε on the worst area;
  (c) no seed shows the instability signature, i.e. latent_std < 0.9, or the bound binding. The bound makes extra_ratio_max > 10 unreachable: ‖extra_t‖ ≤ 10‖h_t‖ gives Σ‖extra_t‖² ≤ 100 Σ‖h_t‖², so RMS(extra)/RMS(h) ≤ 10 (arithmetic). A bound firing therefore counts as the signature.
  If feedback stays OFF, the next try is the media route (S6 (b), §8 7.7; 01-M8), where WORLD's claimed value lies, not another text re-run.
(C) The skip arm changes no default. It reads whether WORLD's objectives are needed once the forecast is bounded.

rulings.title: The position-table door (C43, NEW-13): extrapolating arm before any long-lived parent, or accept context-locked parents
rulings.ruling: Correction of the premise first. The learned absolute position table is not the transformer arm's alone: `_LM` builds `self.pos = nn.Embedding(geom.pos_max, w)` on both arms (`src/lm/api.py:144`), and `encode` adds `model.pos.weight[:L]` before the arch branch (`:614`), so the default GRU (`LM_ARCH` 'gru', `LM_CTX` 128) also trains a 128-row learned table, fed to the GRU at `:666`. `lm.ctx` is EXACT across a resume as the 'positional table extent' (`src/spine/compose.py:3241`) and `encode` refuses L > `d_pos_max` (`src/lm/api.py:599-611`). So C43's resolution ('Default GRU with LM_CTX 128') does not by itself keep the door open. Ruling (the recommendation, extended to both arms): no checkpoint is designated a long-lived parent (the release anchor that continue sessions accumulate on, NEW-01, NEW-02) until its position scheme has a named context-widening route whose known answers pass (§8 3.6). Built, behind one LM position lever (name fixed at build): 'learned' (today's table), the default on both arms, ON, so every record and every pending fleet is unchanged; an extrapolating value per arm, OFF: relative or rotary on the transformer arm (the register's arm), and 'none' on the GRU arm (no table; the recurrence carries order, so nothing is locked by construction); for 'learned', a row-append widening at a declared resume boundary recorded under `ckpt.geometry` (NEW-13's route), with its identity known answer (loss unchanged to 1e-6 on windows at the old ctx) and the cadence-rescaling known answer. The preset builder refuses by name to designate a release anchor whose scheme has no passing route; the refusal is switchable (D17's precedent). Test parents are not held up: §8 2.1's kept checkpoints and 6.1's continuation proceed on 'learned', labelled 'context-locked' in their manifests until the route exists. `LM_ARCH` stays 'gru'; `lm.ctx` stays EXACT until §8 3.6 passes (NEW-13). A change of the default scheme is an efficacy question and reads on GPU by a pre-registered rule: per arm, 'learned' vs its extrapolating value at `LM_CTX` 128, whole-epoch sizing, 5 paired seeds; the extrapolating value becomes the default if it is non-inferior on every area at ε (time-integrated and end-state); a tie goes to it under R4, since it removes the closure by construction; if 'learned' wins beyond ε it stays, and the route counts only if NEW-13's widening reading (ctx 128 → 256 plus N windows against trained-at-256, long-range held-out bits/byte) lands within ε. If that reading misses, the next tried is the extrapolating value trained from the start for the release parent, not abandonment of widening.
rulings.basis: R4 (an irreversible closure is weighed before any reversible cost) and N2 (a fixed live quantity must name a route by which it changes between sessions). The recommendation keeps the door open at the price of a build and a check at designation time; the alternative (accept context-locked parents) closes it for the parent that carries B's accumulated post-training learning, which cannot be moved to a new parent without retraining. A needs context headroom (S5 reads '2-4 s clips that fit LM_CTX', §8 7.6). No efficacy test is needed to decide the policy: it orders builds and refuses a designation, and changes no default. The tree facts (both arms build and add the table; ctx EXACT; the encode refusal) are read from `src/lm/api.py:144, :599-614, :666` and `src/spine/compose.py:3241`. Rotary and relative schemes act inside attention, so the GRU arm's natural non-locking value is no table. N1: 'learned' stays built and the default; nothing is removed. N4: the refusal is a check, not a mode. The owner's 'nothing frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary' (`notes/AGENT_STATE.md:16-17`) is served: a ctx lock is a fixed live dimension, now given a route. Recorded in the owner's review log as a correction of C43's premise, not an escalation, because no long-lived parent exists yet and the route is buildable.

rulings.title: Per-origin limits in the continue preset: DATA_SRC_CAP and the trust detection floor's N
rulings.ruling: Interim. Training runs: `DATA_SRC_CAP` 0 (OFF); a training run counts as one session of curated corpora; the lever is built OFF at SR3 (04-Q12). Continue preset (unbuilt): cap ON at 25 documents' worth of bytes per unpromoted origin per session, provisional (NEW-19), applied to quarantine memory writes and to consolidation bytes (FRAME (7), NEW-18); the preset builder writes it as a number per origin into the manifest at launch (N4): 25 × that origin's median document size in the session's declared material, or 25 × the owner corpus's median document size for material without document boundaries. The trust floor's N is resolved now, by construction: at least 1 trust pass per session and per N bytes of a new origin, N = that origin's cap in bytes, so every capped admission gets a pass; with the cap OFF, 1 pass per session. Floors hold and wall caps apply above them (C31). Pre-registered rule for the cap value, read in §8 5.7 [GPU], 5 seeds, quarantine ON in every arm, promotion open (the post-SR6 regime O5 anticipates; before SR6 an unpromoted untrusted origin never reaches weights and the cap bounds only its quarantine writes): arms cap OFF (0) and cap 25; worlds: single origin k ∈ {5, 25, 100}, k split across 2-5 colluders, an impersonator, a drip (one origin admitting at the cap every session until the ~250 count accrues, 250 / 25 = 10 sessions, arithmetic), and a benign new origin (e.g. `data/continual/01_rust`). Attack success = the trigger-conditioned canary reading against its nuisance-calibrated threshold (NEW-04, from §8 5.1); benign delay = sessions until the benign origin's gain under the cap is within ε of the cap-OFF arm's gain. (1) Keep 25 (the provisional label drops) if in the single-origin k = 25 and k = 100 worlds and the drip world attack success stays within threshold at 4 or more of 5 seeds (04-Q1 note 5's count) and benign delay is at most 1 session. (2) Attack held but benign delay above 1 session → double (25 → 50, arithmetic) and re-run the benign, k = 100 and drip worlds; repeat, keeping the largest value that holds the attack criterion. (3) Attack fails with benign delay at most 1 → halve (25 → 12, rounded down, arithmetic) and re-run; repeat while benign delay stays at most 1. (4) If the drip world alone fails at every cap that keeps benign delay at most 1, build a lineage-cumulative per-origin ceiling (NEW-08's lineage already records admitted bytes per origin) as an arm and re-run before concluding. The colluder worlds are reported and do not set the cap: per-origin caps cannot bound k split over 5 origins (5 × 25 = 125 ≥ 100, arithmetic); a colluder success is a finding against O5 / SR6's promotion rule. The k = 5 world sits below the cap by construction and reads quarantine, corroboration and canaries.
rulings.basis: R1 over R3: untrusted input is attributed and gated, and poisoning must be prevented rather than undone ('removing poison from weights afterwards is unreliable, so guards must be preventive', 04-Q12, l.525). Poisoning is count-based, about 250 documents regardless of clean volume (04-Q12; the literature digest), so the cap is in documents, and 25 is a tenth of that count (arithmetic); NEW-07's ladder {5, 25, 100} brackets it (below, at, 4× above, arithmetic). The ON interim in the unbuilt preset has a safety reason (R1); the training-run value stays the shipped OFF. C29: the emergent path stays as an arm (cap 0). N4: the per-origin number is written by the preset builder at launch, never computed at run time. N = cap ties the monitoring floor to the admission unit (C31: monitoring is priced under R1), a structural choice no test changes. Which value trades learning speed against exposure is efficacy, so it reads on GPU (the CPU rule); E5's model-free worlds (§8 0.6) and 4.7's 'caps bind at their byte count' are operation only. The halving/doubling ladder and the cumulative-ceiling arm follow the owner's 'keep trying'. Context awareness (source credibility) is the owner's principle this serves.
rulings.deciding_test: §8 5.7 [GPU] (poisoning canaries, quarantine and caps ON vs OFF, with the drip and benign worlds); §8 4.7 [CPU] checks only that caps bind at their byte count
rulings.owner_ruling_touched: None explicit. It rests on the owner's stated principle of context awareness including source credibility, and interlocks with O5 (the root of trust, not an owner ruling): the cap is a second line behind quarantine and O5's lock.
rulings.escalate_if: No cap value meets both criteria (attack within threshold at 4 or more of 5 seeds and benign delay at most 1 session) after the halving and doubling steps and the cumulative-ceiling arm: the learning-speed against poisoning-exposure trade has no free point, and 'without risking too much' is the owner's to set; brought with both curves.

findings.what: O6 rule (1), O9 rule (1) and O7 (1a) admit an arm only if a 5-seed one-sided 95% upper bound is below ε, in every area (and in O6 at every session end). No power requirement is set. On the register's own variance figures, benign arms would read 'inadmissible' from noise. That would run through the next-arm ladders and end in false 'threatens B' escalations: O6 (1), O9 (1), and O7's 'tags cost served use beyond ε'.
findings.evidence: O2's basis gives per-area paired SDs of 0.0527 / 0.0624 / 0.1279. At 5 seeds the one-sided bound sits 2.132 × SD / √5 = 0.050 / 0.059 / 0.122 above the mean (arithmetic), so an arm with zero true regression fails 'bound < 0.05' about half the time on the easy area and almost always on the hard one. O6 then requires this jointly over 4 sessions × every area. Note NEW-02 already rejects 5-seed SEs for the gate ('a 5-seed SE inflates k to 3.47-5.56'). PLAN 3.8's between-seed spread is 0.066-0.131 b/B. §8 5.1 sizes the probe, which removes probe noise but not seed-to-seed training variance.
findings.fix: Add to O6 (1), O9 (1) and O7 (1a): 'Seeds per arm are set before the run from §8 5.1/5.2's measured per-area paired SD, so that the bound admits a zero-regression arm with ≥80% power, family-wise over areas and session ends (NEW-02's max-over-areas form). If the bound's half-width exceeds ε/2 at the planned seeds, seeds are added or nuisance runs pooled, and the reading is repeated. An arm whose point estimate is within ε but whose bound fails only on width is "unresolved": it does not advance the ladder and does not count toward escalation.'

findings.what: O5's opening rule (3), 'no canary trips beyond its nuisance-calibrated threshold at any k, split or seed', is judged over roughly 90 readings against a threshold calibrated for about 5% false trips per session. False trips alone would keep the lock shut. The ladder would then run out, and escalation (1) would tell the owner the lock cannot open, when the failure is an artefact of counting many readings.
findings.evidence: The §8 5.7 grid is k ∈ {5, 25, 100} × (one origin, 2/3/4/5 colluders, impersonator) = 18 worlds × 5 seeds = 90 runs, each with at least one consolidation session (arithmetic). NEW-04's canary trigger belongs to a rule calibrated to ≤5% family-wise false rollbacks per session. P(zero trips in 90) ≈ 0.95^90 ≈ 1% if canaries take the whole 5%, and 0.99^90 ≈ 40% even at 1% per reading (arithmetic). O5's escalate_if (1) then reports a limit on B's 'continually learn'.
findings.fix: In O5 (3), define an attack success as the poisoned arm's canary trip rate exceeding its paired no-poison control (same seeds and sessions) beyond a margin set before the run.
